If you’re looking for a **blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (Staffy) puppy near Cardiff**, I’d focus on finding a health-tested breeder rather than choosing purely by colour. Blue Staffies are popular, and the colour can sometimes lead to inflated prices or breeders prioritising appearance over health. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/cardiff?colour=blue&keywords=Working+Chunky&price=1000&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

## Where to look around Cardiff

- **The Royal Kennel Club puppy search** — a good starting point because you can filter Staffordshire Bull Terriers by location and look for breeders who provide health information. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Local Staffy puppy listings around Cardiff/Penarth/Barry/Caerphilly** — there are currently listings advertised in the wider Cardiff area, including blue Staffies, but treat marketplace adverts as leads only and vet the breeder carefully. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/penarth-cardiff?colour=blue&kc_registered=yes&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/cardiff-caerdydd-south-glamorgan?sex=female&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Consider widening the search radius to **South Wales** (e.g., Bridgend, Swansea, Caerphilly, Rhondda Cynon Taf) if you’re willing to wait for the right litter. [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/classifieds/pgofm3el-kc-registered-staffordshire-bull-terrier-puppies-cardiff/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I’d be cautious with anyone who:

- has multiple litters available at once,
- won’t let you see the puppy with its mother,
- wants to meet in a car park or deliver the puppy,
- cannot show health test paperwork,
- focuses mainly on “rare blue” or “XL/chunky” marketing.

## Questions to ask the breeder

### Health testing (very important for Staffies)

Ask:

1. **“Have both parents been health tested? Can I see the certificates?”**

 - Ask specifically about:

 - **L-2-HGA (L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria)** — a neurological condition seen in Staffordshire Bull Terriers.
- **HC-HSF4 hereditary cataracts** — an inherited eye condition.
- Eye screening results.
- Don’t accept “the parents are healthy” as a substitute for testing. Some carriers can look completely normal.
2. **“Can I see the mother with the puppies?”**

 - The dam should be present, comfortable, and interacting normally with the litter.
3. **“Where are the puppies raised?”**

 - Good signs:

 - inside a family environment,
- exposed to normal household sounds,
- handled regularly,
- beginning socialisation.

### About the puppy

Ask:

- “What have you done to socialise the puppies?”
- “Have they met children, other dogs, visitors, household noises?”
- “Which puppy’s temperament suits a first-time owner/family home?”
- “What food are they currently eating?”
- “Have they been wormed and when?”
- “Have they been microchipped?”
- “What vaccinations have they had?”

### About paperwork

Ask for:

- Kennel Club registration details (if advertised as KC registered).
- Microchip information.
- Vaccination record.
- Worming/flea treatment record.
- Written sales contract/health guarantee.
- Copies of parents’ health test results.

## Things I’d ask specifically about a blue Staffy

- “Why did you choose this pairing?”
- “Are you breeding for temperament and health, or mainly colour?”
- “Do either parent have skin problems, allergies, or recurring ear issues?”
- “Have previous puppies from these parents had any health problems?”

## A good sign

A responsible breeder will usually ask **you** questions too — about your home, experience with dogs, work hours, exercise plans, and what life the puppy will have.

If you tell me whether you mean **Cardiff, Wales** and roughly how far you’re willing to travel (e.g., 30 miles, 1–2 hours), I can help narrow the search area and what to check in specific adverts.
